newsitem.title: CHINA: China special economic zones show faster growth.
newsitem.headline: China special economic zones show faster growth.

text.p: The economies of China's four coastal Special Economic Zones grew almost twice as fast as the rest of the country last year but foreign investment slipped, the China Business Times said on Monday.

The average gross domestic product (GDP) growth of the four zones in Shenzhen, which borders Hong Kong, in Zhuhai and Shantou in southern Guangdong province and in Xiamen in eastern Fujian province was 15.16 percent, compared with 9.7 percent nationwide, it said. The total GDP of the four was 177.5 billion yuan ($21.3 billion), it said.
The GDP of Shenzhen alone was 95 billion yuan, accounting for more than half the total, while GDP growth for Shenzhen was 16.4 percent, the newspaper said.
The fastest growing of the four was Xiamen at 19.25 percent while the slowest was Zhuhai with 8.9 percent.

The average industrial output growth of the four zones was 17.49 percent in 1996, with total output valued at 218.9 billion yuan. Shenzhen's industrial output was valued at 120.9 billion yuan, with Xiamen in second place followed by Zhuhai and Shantou.
The fastest growth was registered by Xiamen at 30.27 percent while Shantou was in last place, growing by 9.4 percent.
In terms of foreign trade, the total trade of the four zones was $55.739 billion, a 12.06 percent rise compared with 1995.

Shenzhen accounted for more than half the total, but showed the slowest growth rate of just 0.7 percent. Zhuhai recorded the smallest amount of trade at $4.949 billion but the fastest growth of 30.17 percent.
However, foreign investment fell in the four zones in terms of contracts signed and the investment amount, the newspaper said.
Contracts signed totalled 2,129 in 1996, down 21.93 percent, while their value was $5.948 billion, down 21.59 percent, it said.
Shenzhen posted the biggest drop, with the number of contracts falling by 38.8 percent and the value of investment slashed by 51.5 percent.

But actual foreign investment rose in all four zones, with Shenzhen showing the biggest growth of 56.6 percent and Xiamen the smallest at 2.16 percent, the paper said. Shantou was the only zone to show foreign investment growth in all areas even though it accounted for the smallest proportion, it said.

Average per capita income in the four zones was 9,943.47 yuan last year, it said without giving a comparative figure for 1995. That compared with a national average of 4,380 yuan in 1996, an inflation-adjusted increase of 3.4 percent.
The highest was in Shenzhen where average income was 14,943.5 yuan, followed by Zhuhai with 11,274.7 yuan. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
